einzeiler: How evangelical theology and purity culture trap women in abusive marriages.
kurzfassung: The tragic case of Micah Miller highlights how mainstream evangelical teachings on gender roles and sexual obligation trap women in abusive relationships. Prominent church leaders and marriage books have long taught that a wife's body belongs to her husband, fostering environments where predators can thrive with impunity. This systemic indoctrination trains victims to distrust their own instincts and blame themselves for failing their abusers.
stichpunkte: J.P. Miller subjected his wife Micah to extreme psychological, physical, and sexual abuse.
J.P.'s abusive theological views on gender and a wife's sexual duties mirror mainstream evangelical teachings.
Best-selling Christian marriage books instruct wives that denying their husbands sex is sinful.
Data shows 40% of surveyed evangelical women believe wives must provide sex on demand to prevent infidelity.
Evangelical purity culture teaches women that their bodies belong to others rather than themselves.
Victims of abuse internalize self-doubt because church doctrine tells them human hearts are inherently wicked.
Prominent evangelical figures like John Piper and John MacArthur discourage victims from leaving abusive marriages.
The institutional church's protection of abusive leaders mirrors its broader political alignments with powerful men.
